CHIEF COMPLAINT
Followup of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male presenting for followup of depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension. He reports it has been a challenging year and a half. He experienced significant anxiety and stress in preparation for Thanksgiving, though the holiday itself was positive after not seeing family for about two years. He is planning to take a vacation to somewhere warm in the new year. Regarding his depression, he tried a new strategy over the summer by taking long walks outside every morning, which he found beneficial with the nice weather and blooming plants. This also motivated weekend yard work and outdoor activity. However, with the changing seasons and cold weather, he has been unable to continue this routine and is seeking alternative strategies. He denies thoughts of self-harm or harming others. Regarding his diabetes, he managed reasonably well through Halloween but did not strictly adhere to his diet during Thanksgiving week. He is currently monitoring his intake more carefully. For his hypertension, he purchased a blood pressure cuff as recommended and reports readings have been moderate with nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, blood in stool, or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (currently on, to be increased), lisinopril 20 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports recent stress related to holiday planning and family gatherings. Planning vacation. Previously engaged in outdoor morning walks and light yard work as exercise and stress management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure good, in normal range. Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated. Heart: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at left base (previously noted). Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in lower extremities.

RESULTS
EKG: No acute concerns noted. Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0% (elevated; goal <6%). Lipid panel: Ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. Patient prefers non-medication management at this time.
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8%. Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1C in 2 months. Order lipid panel.
3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order echocardiogram to reevaluate heart murmur and cardiac function. Blood pressure control currently adequate.
